items.Sentence: Raw sewage first enters the septage receiving station where it’s mixed with air in the septage holding tanks.
received at the headworks, where it’s passed through a grit chamber to separate solid particles.

mixed with activated sludge in the mixed liquor structure, and it is subsequently directed to a 170 feet (ft) x 124 ft Biolac���� aeration basin where air is once again introduced into the sewage water.
Wastewater discharged from the Biolac���� aeration basin is then passed through two (2) secondary clarifiers (40 ft x 43 ft) in parallel.
Sludge collected from the secondary clarifiers is dewatered at a rotary drum thickener
then pumped to six (6) sludge drying beds (three (3) sludge beds measuring 70 ft x 38 ft and three (3) more measuring 92 ft x 40 ft).
The sludge drying beds are equipped with sand filters and perforated underdrains.
There is an option for the use of a secondary effluent pump station and continuous backwash upflow filter if deemed necessary by the operational staff.
The wastewater from the secondary clarifiers flows through a ultraviolet (UV) disinfection system and an effluent flow metering system before being discharged to the Pear Drain.
After drying, the sludge is hauled away to a farm in Arizona.
